question: What is the primary function of the pulmonary circulation?

options.A: To supply systemic organs with nutrients
options.B: To transport deoxygenated blood to the lungs and oxygenated blood to the left heart
options.C: To maintain high blood pressure throughout the body
options.D: To pump oxygenated blood directly to the right atrium

explanation: Pulmonary circulation specifically moves deoxygenated blood from the right side of the heart to the lungs for gas exchange and returns oxygenated blood to the left side of the heart. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h1)

question: Why does the pulmonary circulation operate under a lower pressure system compared to the systemic circulation?

options.A: To prevent damage to the delicate alveolar-capillary membranes
options.B: To increase the speed of red blood cells
options.C: To force more carbon dioxide into the tissues
options.D: To compensate for a weaker left ventricle

explanation: The lower pressure in the pulmonary circuit protects the delicate alveolar-capillary membranes in the lungs from physical damage during gas exchange. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h1)

question: Through which valve does blood pass when moving from the right atrium to the right ventricle?
explanation: The tricuspid valve separates the right atrium from the right ventricle, ensuring one-way blood flow. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h2)

question: How many pulmonary veins typically empty oxygenated blood into the left atrium?
explanation: Four main pulmonary veins—two coming from each lung—empty freshly oxygenated blood into the left atrium. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h2)

question: Which heart valve opens to allow deoxygenated blood to flow from the right ventricle into the pulmonary trunk?
explanation: The pulmonary semilunar valve opens during right ventricular contraction to let blood enter the pulmonary trunk. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h3)

question: What makes pulmonary arteries unique compared to most other arteries in the adult body?

options.B: They have the thickest muscular walls
options.C: They transport blood directly to systemic organs
options.D: They operate under the highest systemic pressure

explanation: Pulmonary arteries are unique because they carry deoxygenated blood away from the heart toward the lungs, whereas all other systemic arteries carry oxygenated blood. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h3)

question: What drives the movement of oxygen and carbon dioxide across the alveolar-capillary membrane?

options.C: Direct pumping by the left atrium

explanation: Gases move across the membrane via simple passive diffusion down their respective partial pressure gradients. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h4)

question: How does pneumonia or pulmonary edema typically affect the alveolar-capillary membrane?

options.A: It thickens the membrane and impairs gas diffusion
options.B: It eliminates the capillary bed entirely
options.C: It converts the membrane into active transport pumps
options.D: It decreases the surface area to zero

explanation: Fluid accumulation or inflammation thickens the alveolar-capillary membrane, increasing diffusion distance and leading to impaired gas exchange. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h4)

question: What is unique about the pulmonary veins in adults?

options.A: They carry deoxygenated blood to the lungs
options.B: They carry oxygenated blood to the left atrium
options.C: They possess the thickest muscular walls in the body
options.D: They connect directly to the right ventricle

explanation: Pulmonary veins are unique because they are the only veins in the adult body carrying oxygen-rich blood back to the heart. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h5)

question: Blood flowing from the left atrium into the left ventricle passes through which valve?
explanation: The mitral (or bicuspid) valve regulates blood flow between the left atrium and the left ventricle. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h5)

question: What is a major reason why pulmonary blood pressure is much lower than systemic blood pressure?

options.A: The pulmonary vessels have high resistance and narrow lumens
options.B: The pulmonary vascular bed has low resistance due to compliant, wide vessels
options.C: The right ventricle pumps with much more force than the left ventricle
options.D: Gravity pulls all blood away from the lungs

explanation: The pulmonary vessels are wide, short, and highly compliant, creating a low-resistance pathway that keeps pulmonary blood pressure low. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h6)

question: How do local pulmonary arterioles respond to hypoxia in a specific area of the lung?

options.A: They dilate to increase local blood flow
options.B: They constrict to redirect blood to well-ventilated areas
options.C: They rupture to release trapped gases

explanation: Hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction causes vessels in poorly ventilated areas to constrict, optimizing ventilation-perfusion matching. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h6)

question: What is a common origin of a pulmonary embolism (PE)?

options.A: Deep vein thrombosis in the lower extremities
options.B: Thrombus formation inside the left atrium

explanation: Pulmonary emboli frequently originate as blood clots (deep vein thrombosis) in the veins of the lower limbs that break loose and travel to the lungs. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h7)

question: Chronically elevated pressure in the pulmonary arteries primarily places excessive workload on which heart chamber?
explanation: Pulmonary hypertension increases the workload of the right ventricle, which must pump against higher resistance, potentially leading to cor pulmonale. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h7)
